event.description: Share one query output row across depth blocks
event.proposal: family: attention organization; current retained incumbent is 2781 parameters at 100.0000%, a +1.00 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family most recent accepted result: attempt-0066, one head-local attention output map shared across depth at 2781 parameters and 100.00%; same-family most recent failed result: attempt-0067, both head-local output maps shared across depth at 2732 parameters and 9.42%; prior attempts in this family: 14. Hypothesis: the 49-parameter second-head output tie crossed a capacity boundary, so test a smaller parameterization-preserving tie: share only one 14-value query-output row between the two depth blocks, with the remaining 13 query rows, both MQA K/V maps, and all head-local output maps independent. This removes 14 parameters for a target of 2767. It is more informative than the nearest untested one-row K/V tie because query sharing tests depth redundancy in attention-score formation while preserving the complete value path; it also probes a finer boundary immediately below the accepted output-map tie. Keep d14/h2/L2 MQA, ff23 with one within-block tied hidden unit shared across blocks, rank8 positions, two final group scales, reversed operands, zero weight decay, mixed-digit curriculum, and 30000 steps; retain only official accuracy at least 99% and strictly fewer parameters than the incumbent.
